problem: End-to-end RL and modular ObjectNav systems explore large, semantically diverse unseen scenes without any prior about layout, so exploration is slow and unfocused and success stays around 50% even for the SOTA. Sim-to-real transfer for such policies is also hard.
motivation: Humans search for objects by reasoning about room types (e.g. a sink is in a bathroom). Giving the agent cheap landmarks (room centers and types, with no obstacle or object map) can make exploration semantically focused. Skills trained separately with RL are also more robust to noisy semantics than map-based planning.
key_idea: Give the agent room-center landmarks with room types, rank rooms by object-room statistics and distance, and run a hierarchy of separately RL-trained skills (PointNav to the room, Explore inside it, GoalReacher to a seen object).
insight: Landmark knowledge is the main gain: HLPO reaches 0.75 success with GT semantics versus 0.51 for Auxiliary RL, and 0.46 versus 0.20 with learned semantics. Replacing the RL skills with map-based planning (HLPO Plan) lowers success (0.68 / 0.37), while giving the agent an obstacle map (HLPO Map) raises it to 0.90 / 0.61. This suggests RL skills are more robust to segmentation noise and map errors than planners, and that navigation to the landmark is still a bottleneck.
method: Landmarks: list of all room center coordinates and room types given to the agent, with no obstacle map and no object information.
Global policy: uses room-object statistics from training scenes to rank rooms by probability of containing the goal object divided by distance to the room.
Data preparation: SOLOv2 semantic segmentation and a depth-reconstruction network (used on the real Husky robot, which has only an RGB camera).
PointNav skill (RL, DD-PPO): navigates to the chosen room center, with a Fast Marching Method planner tested as an alternative.
Explore skill (RL): explores the nearby area until the agent leaves the room.
GoalReacher skill (RL): activates when the goal category is seen in the semantic mask, approaches the object and stops.
Scene reconstruction for sim-to-real: the lab was scanned with a Leica RTC360, textured in RealityCapture and loaded in Habitat for fine-tuning before Husky tests.

setting.backbone: Three PPO/DD-PPO-trained RL skill policies (ResNet9 + LSTM/GRU), SOLOv2 segmentation, depth-estimation net, and a rule/statistics-based global policy
setting.training_data: Matterport3D scenes in Habitat for each skill; PointNav trained in the faster BPS simulator; small additional training in a reconstructed lab scene for real transfer
setting.observation: RGB-D camera + GPS/compass + list of room landmarks (center coordinates and type); real robot uses RGB only, with depth reconstructed
setting.action_space: discrete: forward, turn left, turn right, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes; BPS simulator for PointNav training)
setting.privileged: GT room landmarks (centers and types) given at test time; GT semantics in the main setting; the HLPO (Map) variant additionally gets the obstacle map

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 episodes in test MP3D scenes, geodesic distance to goal at least 5 m
numbers.backbone: RL skills (PointNav, Explore, GoalReacher) with GT semantic sensor
numbers.extra: Uses GT room landmarks; results averaged over three runs with dispersion at most 0.03

numbers_note: Success and SoftSPL are printed as fractions (0.75), not percentages. Table 1 gives the learned-semantic HLPO (Map) row as SR 0.61, SoftSPL 0.42. Standard SPL is not reported, and the test set is a custom 100-episode set, so the numbers are not directly comparable to the official challenge results.
results: HLPO reaches 0.75 success (GT semantics) and 0.46 (learned semantics), well above Auxiliary RL (0.51 / 0.19), 2RL (0.46 / 0.20) and SemExp (0.24 / 0.11). The comparison is on a custom 100-episode MP3D test set, and HLPO has access to landmarks that the baselines lack. The method was also confirmed on a Husky robot in a reconstructed lab scene, with SPL 0.8 in simulation from five start points.
limitations: Requires privileged room landmarks (centers and types), so the comparison with baselines is not on equal information.
Small evaluation set (100 episodes), a non-standard metric set (SoftSPL, no plain SPL), and a large gap remains between GT and learned semantics.
The real-world test is limited to one reconstructed lab scene, and the skills use discrete actions.
